surface_mechanism_description: The atomic hydrogen produced in a rf source is reactive enough to remove halogens from the surface effectively even at a very low growth temperature. The extraction reaction of Cl by atomic H occurs even at room temperature with high efficiency, producing metallic films. Since the atomic H has a high enough reducing power to produce metal-Ta films, the nitrogen is then readily incorporated into the film to produce cubic TaN.
evidence: Our previous report on PE-ALD Ti and Ta has shown that the atomic hydrogen produced in a rf source is reactive enough to remove halogens from the surface effectively even at a very low growth temperature. The extraction reaction of Cl by atomic H occurs even at room temperature with high efficiency, producing metallic films. Since the atomic H has a high enough reducing power to produce metal–Ta films, the nitrogen is then readily incorporated into the film to produce cubic TaN.
